dialogues.speaker: Shahbandar
dialogues.text: Halva, did you lower tax rates for the merchants again?

dialogues.speaker: Shahbandar
dialogues.text: I told you, don't be afraid to disagree with them. You have to be patient with them, and use the old carrot-and-stick approach...

dialogues.speaker: Halva
dialogues.text: Uh, with all due respect, I don't think that's the problem...

dialogues.speaker: Halva
dialogues.text: The majority of the taxes and fees we collect end up as funding for the researchers, but the Akademiya is hardly strapped for cash.

dialogues.speaker: Halva
dialogues.text: But putting undue pressure on the merchants isn't conducive to the normal flow of business. So, it doesn't hurt to be more lenient with them...

dialogues.speaker: Shahbandar
dialogues.text: Don't be naïve! I'll remind you that your job is to collect taxes and fees, not to promote business.

dialogues.speaker: Shahbandar
dialogues.text: There are other ways of regulating such business matters. It's nothing we of the Navbed need to concern ourselves with.

dialogues.speaker: Shahbandar
dialogues.text: You're still an intern, so all you need to do is the job you've been tasked with. Understood?

dialogues.speaker: Halva
dialogues.text: Heh, I wonder what new stock the shop's got in today...!

dialogues.speaker: Halva
dialogues.text: Ah, no. I'm just admiring them is all.

dialogues.speaker: Halva
dialogues.text: I may not be able to afford anything like this as a trainee tax officer, but just being able to look at such shiny and beautiful things brings me joy.

dialogues.speaker: Halva
dialogues.text: *sigh* It's hard not to doubt yourself when your superior is always scolding you for being childish...

dialogues.speaker: Halva
dialogues.text: So, when I'm not working, I look at the things I like to blow off steam.

dialogues.speaker: Halva
dialogues.text: Later, I'm gonna look around some more.
